Partnership Activations at Kalshi: what success looks like.

A partnership is a contract until fans can see it, feel it and use it. I turn rights into moments, and moments into new users.

A short, personal take on the role: how I'd spend the first 90 days, three activations I'd pitch, and how I'd prove they worked.

What the role is really for

Turn rights into moments.

How I read the job

Every league, creator and media deal comes with rights. This role makes sure each one shows up where fans are, feels native to the moment, and ends in someone opening Kalshi.

What success looks like in a year
01

No right left on the table

Every partnership has an activation plan, an owner and a calendar, and the rights we pay for get used, not just listed.

02

Every activation is measurable

Each moment ships with its own link, code or QR, so we can tie it to sign-ups and first trades and compare it fairly with paid channels.

03

A playbook the team can repeat

A tested format for watch parties, creator moments and on-site lounges, with board-ready reporting and partners who want to renew and do more.

Three activations I'd pitch

Big moments, built for Kalshi.

These are my proposals, not existing Kalshi plans. They build on partnerships Kalshi has announced publicly (the US Open, the NBA, the Pro Padel League) and would run with Legal and Compliance from day one.
First 90 days

Learn, ship, then scale.

How I'd measure it

Proof, not vibes.

With RISE, I built a sponsorship ROI model for women's sports brands: a way to show what an activation actually returned, not just how it looked. At Kalshi I'd apply the same logic, tracing each moment from the room to the first trade.
